[languages] 'lin', 'kon', 'lua', and 'swa' are recognized as national languages and treated here as 'regional'.
[languages] The sign language used is presumed to be 'fsl' (Francophone African Sign Language), used informally.

LABEL: Central African Republic
NOTES: [languages] 'fra' and 'sgb' are both official languages according to the 2004 Constitution (Article 9).
[languages] 'csf' (Langue des signes française) is used informally in education and religious contexts,
but is not officially recognized.
[languages] No linguistic communities reach the threshold for 'extraTerritorialCommunities'.

LABEL: Congo
NOTES: [languages] 'fra' is the only official language by law (de jure).
[languages] 'lin' and 'kon' are national languages with geographically formalized use and institutional
functions; classified as 'regional'.
[languages] 'fcs' (Langue des signes française) is used informally, without official recognition.
[languages] No qualifying 'extraTerritorialCommunities' currently documented.

LABEL: Switzerland

[languages] No qualifying 'extraTerritorialCommunities' currently documented.

LABEL: Côte d'Ivoire
NOTES: [languages] 'fra' is the only official language recognized by the Constitution (Art. 1).
[languages] Languages like 'dyu', 'aka', and 'kro' are widely spoken across regions and serve as lingua francas.
[languages] 'fcs' (Langue des signes française) is used without legal status.
[languages] 'nqo' refers to a writing system, not a spoken language; its inclusion should be qualified.
[languages] No documented 'extraTerritorialCommunities' currently apply.

LABEL: Cook Islands
NOTES: [languages] 'eng' and 'rar' are the official languages under the Cook Islands Constitution (Art. 64).
[languages] 'tzh' is a recognized orthographic variant of Rarotongan but not a separate official language.
[languages] Local languages like 'pkp', 'mri', and 'tah' are spoken by communities with ancestral links, but lack legal status.
[languages] No sign language is currently documented with formal status.
[languages] No documented 'extraTerritorialCommunities' currently apply.

LABEL: Chile

text.spa: Por la razón o la fuerza

NOTES: [languages] 'spa' is the only official language per Chilean legislation.
[languages] Languages such as 'arn' (Mapudungun), 'rap' (Rapa Nui), 'aym' (Aymara), and others are used by Indigenous communities but do not hold official status.
[languages] 'csg' (Chilean Sign Language) is used informally and recognized in educational and cultural settings, but lacks full legal status.
[languages] No documented 'extraTerritorialCommunities' currently apply.

LABEL: Cameroon
NOTES: [languages] Cameroon has two de jure official languages: French and English.
[languages] Numerous indigenous languages like 'ffm', 'nmg', 'bkm', and 'bcu' are widely spoken, often used in media and education locally.
[languages] Several regional languages such as 'bas', 'dua', and 'bss' represent long-standing ethnolinguistic communities.
[languages] 'csn' (Cameroonian Sign Language) is used by deaf communities, but not officially recognized.
[languages] No qualifying 'extraTerritorialCommunities' currently documented.

LABEL: China
NOTES: [languages] 'cmn' (Mandarin) is the sole de jure official language in China.
[languages] Several Sinitic languages like 'yue' (Cantonese), 'wuu' (Shanghainese), and 'nan' (Hokkien)
are widely spoken regionally but lack official recognition.
[languages] Numerous minority languages such as 'uig' (Uyghur), 'bod' (Tibetan), and 'zha' (Zhuang) are
spoken by recognized ethnic groups but often face sociopolitical restrictions.
[languages] 'csl' (Chinese Sign Language) is used by the deaf community but is not formally recognized.
[ccIdn] Two internationalized domains are available: .中国 (Simplified) and .中國 (Traditional), with
differing region usage.

LABEL: Colombia
NOTES: [languages] 'spa' (Spanish) is the only de jure official language, according to the Colombian Constitution.
[languages] Indigenous languages such as 'way' (Wayuu), 'pbb' (Páez), and 'iku' (Arhuaco) are
constitutionally protected and used in native communities.
[languages] 'csn' (Colombian Sign Language) is commonly used but has limited official support.
[mottos] 'Libertad y Orden' is the national motto, used on official symbols such as the coat of arms.

LABEL: Costa Rica

text.spa: ¡Vivan siempre el trabajo y la paz!

NOTES: [languages] 'spa' (Spanish) is the sole official language of Costa Rica as per the Constitution.
[languages] Indigenous and Afro-Caribbean languages like 'bzd' (Bribri), 'gnr' (Guaymí), and 'emp'
(Emberá) are spoken in specific communities.
[languages] 'csr' (Costa Rican Sign Language) is commonly used but not formally recognized.
[mottos] '¡Vivan siempre el trabajo y la paz!' is the official national motto, appearing on the coat of arms.

LABEL: Cuba
NOTES: [languages] 'spa' (Spanish) is the only official language of Cuba, enshrined in the Constitution.
[languages] 'hat' (Haitian Creole) and 'yua' (Yucatec Maya) are spoken by localized communities of
Haitian and Mayan descent.
[languages] 'csl' (Cuban Sign Language) is used in practice but lacks formal recognition.
[mottos] The motto '¡Patria o Muerte, Venceremos!' is used officially and tied to revolutionary ideology.

LABEL: Cabo Verde
NOTES: [languages] 'por' (Portuguese) is the only official language of Cabo Verde, constitutionally established.
[languages] 'kea' (Kabuverdianu) is widely spoken in everyday life and media, but lacks formal official status.
[mottos] The national motto 'Unidade, Trabalho, Progresso' is official and widely used in national symbols.

LABEL: Curaçao
NOTES: [languages] Dutch, Papiamento, and English are co-official languages of Curaçao, established in legal and
educational frameworks.
[languages] Spanish is present due to regional and economic proximity, classified under local communities.
[mottos] 'Je maintiendrai' is the royal motto of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, used symbolically in Curaçao.
[dialCodes] +5999 is formally assigned to Curaçao under ITU regulations.

LABEL: Christmas Island
NOTES: [languages] English is the only official language under Australian jurisdiction.
[languages] Mandarin Chinese and Malay are widely spoken due to community composition.
[signs] 'aus' (Australian Sign Language) is used without formal recognition.
[dialCodes] +61891 is assigned under Australian jurisdiction and used de facto in Christmas Island.
Calls are routed via Australian infrastructure.
[mottos] No official or historical motto is currently designated for the territory.

LABEL: Cyprus
NOTES: [languages] Greek and Turkish are the only official languages recognized in the Constitution of Cyprus.
[languages] English is widely spoken in public administration and education.
[languages] The presence of Armenian, French, Arabic (Cypriot Maronite Arabic), Syriac, and Italian
communities is acknowledged, but without official status.
[signs] 'csg' (Cypriot Sign Language) is in use but lacks formal recognition.
[dialCodes] +357 is the de jure international calling code for the Republic of Cyprus.
[mottos] No official or historical motto is currently designated.

LABEL: Czechia
NOTES: [languages] Czech ('ces') is the only official language enshrined in the Constitution.
[languages] Slovak ('slk') is recognized as regional due to historical and cultural ties.
[languages] German ('deu') and English ('eng') are widely spoken, especially in tourism and education.
[languages] Roma ('rom') is a historical local community; Polish ('pol'), Russian ('rus'), Ukrainian
('ukr'), and Vietnamese ('vie') are classified as extraTerritorialCommunities based on recent
immigration patterns.
[signs] 'cse' (Czech Sign Language) is used but not officially recognized.
[dialCodes] +420 is the de jure and de facto international calling code for Czechia.
[mottos] 'Pravda vítězí' is the official motto of Czechia and appears on the presidential standard.

LABEL: Germany
NOTES: [languages] German ('deu') is the only official language at federal level.
[languages] Danish ('dan'), Frisian ('frr'), Low German ('nds'), and Alemannic ('gsw') have recognized
regional or minority status.
[languages] Turkish ('tur') and English ('eng') are widely spoken, particularly in education and
immigrant communities.
[languages] Roma ('rom') and Kölsch ('ksh') are locally rooted communities.
[languages] Polish ('pol'), Russian ('rus'), Ukrainian ('ukr'), and Vietnamese ('vie') represent
extraTerritorialCommunities.
[signs] 'gsg' (German Sign Language) is commonly used but not officially codified nationally.

It includes varieties such as Kabyle (kab), Mozabite (mzb), Tamasheq (tmh), and Tamahaq (taq),
all part of the broader Berber (ber) language family.
[languages] No regional languages are legally defined despite strong local usage of Berber varieties.
[languages] No immigrant languages meet the threshold or public visibility for inclusion as
extraTerritorialCommunities.

LABEL: Ecuador
NOTES: [languages] Ecuador recognizes both Spanish and Kichwa (que) as official languages, and Shuar as a
language of intercultural relations.
[languages] The variant Kichwa of the Sierra (qug) has regional status.
[languages] Numerous indigenous languages are spoken by local communities, including Cofán (cof),
Waorani (wao), Achuar (ach), Shuar (shp), and others.

LABEL: Estonia
NOTES: [languages] Russian and English are widely spoken, especially in urban and border regions.
[languages] Võro (vro) is a recognized traditional variety with limited regional support but no formal legal status.
[languages] Other languages like German, Ukrainian, Finnish and Romani are present among local communities or minorities.

LABEL: Egypt
NOTES: [languages] Modern Standard Arabic (arb) is the sole official language by law.
[languages] Egyptian Arabic (arz) and Sa'idi Arabic (enb) are widely spoken regional varieties.
[languages] Coptic (cop) has liturgical use, while Nubian (nob), Beja (bej), Greek (grc), and Armenian
(arm) reflect historical communities.
[languages] No regional languages are formally recognized; all minority languages lack legal status.
[languages] Despite hosting migrant and refugee populations from the Horn of Africa and beyond, Egypt
has no immigrant language community that meets visibility or population thresholds for inclusion.

LABEL: Western Sahara
NOTES: [languages] Arabic (arb) and Spanish (spa) are declared official by the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic,
but only Arabic has de facto use in administration and daily life.
[languages] Hassaniya Arabic (mey) is the primary spoken variety.
[languages] Berber (ber) presence is historical but not widespread; no legal status is conferred.
[languages] Due to the political status of Western Sahara, language policy and recognition remain disputed
and vary across territories administered by Morocco and the SADR.
[dialCodes] The country code +212 is officially assigned to Morocco and used de facto in Western Sahara.
[ccTld] The .eh domain is officially reserved for Western Sahara but remains undelegated and inactive
due to the ongoing territorial dispute.

LABEL: Eritrea
NOTES: [languages] Eritrea has no constitutionally defined official language. Tigrinya, Arabic, and English are
all used in administration, though only Tigrinya and Arabic have strong community roots.
[languages] Tigre (tig) is widely spoken, especially in the western and northern regions.
[languages] Local communities use several other native languages, including Bilen (byn), Nara (nrb),
Saho (ssy), Kunama (kun), and Blin (blu), as well as immigrant or border languages such as Amharic (amh)
and Oromo (orm).
[languages] The multiplicity of languages is recognized in practice but not formalized legally.
[languages] English is used in education and government but lacks strong community roots.
[languages] Italian (ita) persists historically but has no institutional role today.

LABEL: Spain
NOTES: [languages] Spanish (spa) is the sole official language of the state, while Catalan (cat), Basque (eus),
Galician (glg), and Aranese/Occitan (oci) are co-official in their respective autonomous communities.
[languages] Several regional or minority languages have cultural recognition but no official status,
including Asturian (ast), Extremaduran (ext), and Aragonese (arn).
[languages] Other traditional varieties or revived dialects like Mozarabic (mzc), Leonese (ltg),
Caló (rml), Patués (pov), Malagueño (mlg), and Fala (fab) are documented at local levels.
[languages] Spanish Sign Language (ssp) is used throughout the country but lacks full legal
recognition nationally.
[languages] Spain hosts numerous immigrant language communities, notably Arabic (ara), Romanian (ron),
Quechua (que), Tigrinya (tir), Wolof (zul), Polish (pol), Portuguese (por), French (fra), Urdu (urd),
and Chinese (zho), some of which are demographically and socially significant.

LABEL: Ethiopia
NOTES: [languages] Amharic (amh) is the sole federal working language of Ethiopia and holds official status
nationally.
[languages] Several regional languages are widely spoken and used in education or local administration,
including Oromo (orm), Tigrinya (tir), Somali (som), Sidamo (sid), and Wolaytta (wal).
[languages] The constitution grants regions the right to establish their own working languages, resulting
in a linguistically federal system.
[languages] Classical Ge'ez (gez) remains a liturgical language in the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.
[languages] Ethiopian Sign Language (eth) is used within deaf communities but lacks formal recognition
at the federal level.

LABEL: Finland
NOTES: [languages] Finnish (fin) and Swedish (swe) are the two official national languages of Finland by
constitutional law.
[languages] Finland-Swedish Sign Language (fss) is recognized as a distinct sign language associated with
the Swedish-speaking minority, but has no regional official status.
[languages] Russian (rus), Estonian (est), and English (eng) are widely spoken by immigrant and
international communities.
[languages] Several Sámi languages such as Northern (sme), Skolt (sms), and Inari Sámi (smn) have
official status in designated Sámi homeland areas.
[languages] Finnish Sign Language (fse) is used widely within the deaf community and is legally recognized.
[languages] Finland hosts immigrant communities speaking Arabic (ara), Somali (som), Kurdish (kur),
Persian (fao), and Tigrinya (tir), particularly in urban centers.

LABEL: Fiji

text.fij: Rerevaka na Kalou ka Doka na Tui

NOTES: [languages] English (eng), Fijian (fij), and Fiji Hindi (hif) are co-official languages as per the
2013 Constitution.
[languages] Fijian Sign Language (fji) is recognized for official communication with the deaf community.
[languages] Gilbertese (gil) and Tongan (ton) are spoken by local Pacific islander minorities.
[languages] Bauan Fijian (bau) is the standard dialect of Fijian used in formal and educational contexts.

LABEL: Falkland Islands (Malvinas)
NOTES: [dependency] The Falkland Islands (Malvinas) are a British Overseas Territory claimed by Argentina.
[languages] English (eng) is the only official language and the primary language of daily life.
[dialCodes] The international dialing code +500 is uniquely assigned to the Falkland Islands.

LABEL: Micronesia (Federated States of)
NOTES: [languages] English (eng) is the sole official language at the federal level, while local indigenous
languages are used at state and community levels.
[languages] Chuukese (chk), Pohnpeian (pon), Kosraean (kos), and Yapese (yap) are widely spoken within
their respective states.
[languages] Additional local Micronesian languages include Ulithian (uli), Tobian (tox), Woleaian (woe),
Puluwatese (fud), Kapingamarangi (kpg), Mortlockese (mrl), and Pingelapese (poh).

LABEL: Faroe Islands
NOTES: [dependency] The Faroe Islands are a self-governing archipelago under the sovereignty of the Kingdom
of Denmark.
[languages] Faroese (fao) is the primary spoken language and official together with Danish (dan).
[dialCodes] The international dialing code +298 is uniquely assigned to the Faroe Islands.

LABEL: France
NOTES: [languages] French (fra) is the only official language nationwide, with several regional languages
recognized for cultural and educational use.
[languages] Languages such as Occitan (oci), Breton (bre), Corsican (cor), Alsatian (gsw), Catalan (cat),
Basque (eus), and Galician (glg) are historically and regionally significant.
[languages] Large immigrant communities speak Arabic (ara), Portuguese (por), Italian (ita),
Mandarin Chinese (cmn), and others, some with significant demographic presence.
[languages] French Sign Language (fsl) is officially recognized for communication with the deaf community.

LABEL: Gabon
NOTES: [languages] French (fra) is the only official language of Gabon.
[languages] Gabon is home to over 40 living indigenous Bantu languages; although none carries official
status, they remain essential to community identity.
[languages] Fang (fan) is the most widely spoken indigenous language and functions as a lingua franca,
especially in northern regions and Libreville.
[languages] Other languages like Myene (mye), Punu (pun), Nzebi (nzb), Teke (tte), Kota, and Baka are
spoken by specific ethnic groups and are at various stages of vitality or endangerment.
[languages] French remains dominant in public life; many indigenous languages face decline as younger
generations adopt French.

LABEL: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

officialName.eng: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

NOTES: [languages] English (eng) is the only official language de jure at the national level.
[languages] Welsh (cym), Scottish Gaelic (gla), Irish (gle), Cornish (cor), Scots (sco), and
Ulster Scots (uln) are recognized regionally within their respective territories.
[languages] Large immigrant communities speak Urdu (urd), Punjabi (pan), Gujarati (guj), Bengali (ben),
Arabic (ara), Polish (pol), Somali (som), Tigrinya (tir), Turkish (tur), Pashto (pus), and Romani (rom).
[languages] Extra-territorial communities maintain active use of Hindi (hin), Tamil (tam), Swahili (swa),
French (fra), Chinese (zho), and Italian (ita), primarily among second-generation diaspora groups.
[languages] British Sign Language (bfi) is officially recognized in the UK.

LABEL: Grenada

text.eng: Ever Conscious of God We Aspire, Build and Advance as One People

NOTES: [languages] English (eng) is the sole official language of Grenada.
[languages] Grenadian Creole English (gcl) is widely spoken as a vernacular.
[languages] American Sign Language (bzs) is used within the Deaf community.

LABEL: Georgia
NOTES: [languages] Georgian (kat) is the sole official language de jure.
[languages] Abkhaz (abk) has official status in the Autonomous Republic of Abkhazia.
[languages] Russian (rus), Azerbaijani (azj), and Armenian (arm) are widely spoken in specific regions.
[languages] Minority communities speak Avar (ava), Kabardian (kbd), Lezgi (lez), Chechen (che),
and Udmurt (udm).

LABEL: French Guiana
NOTES: [languages] French (fra) is the sole official language de jure.
[languages] French Guianese Creole (gcr) is widely spoken among the population.
[languages] Indigenous and immigrant communities speak Carib (car), Wayampi (way), Lokono (mpy),
Tupinambá (tup), Tiriyó (tir), Palikur (poi), Ndyuka (njo), Dutch (dut), Sranan Tongo (srn), and Tem (tem).

LABEL: Guernsey
NOTES: [languages] Guernésiais (nrf) is a Norman language variety spoken by a small segment of the local
population.
[currencies] The Guernsey pound (GGP) is issued by the States of Guernsey and is used alongside GBP
at parity. It is legal tender within the bailiwick but not generally accepted elsewhere.
It is not inside the list for the ISO-4217 codes

LABEL: Ghana
NOTES: [languages] English is the sole official language of Ghana, used in government, education, and media.
[languages] English has full legal status and is mandated for use in all branches of the state, including
courts, parliament, and public administration.
[languages] Akan (aka/twi) and Ewe (ewe) are among the most widely spoken indigenous languages, with
numerous others playing key roles in specific regions.
[languages] Ghana recognizes 11 government-sponsored languages used in education and cultural preservation.

LABEL: Gibraltar
NOTES: [mottos] The Latin phrase 'Nulli Expugnabilis Hosti' (Military) appears on Gibraltar's coat of arms and
is widely considered its military motto.
[languages] Spanish is widely spoken due to geographic proximity and cultural contact with Andalusia.
[languages] Local language Llanito (lld) is an Andalusian Spanish-English creole unique to Gibraltar.

LABEL: Greenland
NOTES: [languages] Greenlandic (Kalaallisut) is the only official language of Greenland since 2009.
[languages] Danish is a recognized regional and working language, especially in education and government.
[languages] The three main dialects of Greenlandic are: Kalaallisut (klq), Tunumiisut (ktq), and Inuktun (gdn).

LABEL: Gambia
NOTES: [languages] English is the only official language of The Gambia, with full de jure status.
[languages] Several Niger–Congo languages are widely spoken, including Wolof, Fula, and Mandinka.
[languages] The category 'localCommunities' includes varieties and dialects of major ethnolinguistic groups.

LABEL: Guinea
NOTES: [languages] French is the official language of Guinea by constitutional mandate.
[languages] Widely spoken indigenous languages include Fula (fuf), Susu (sus), and Mandinka (man).
[languages] Local community languages reflect ethnic diversity, including Djallonké (djz), N'Ko (nqo),
and others.

LABEL: Guadeloupe
NOTES: [languages] French is the sole official language in Guadeloupe as an overseas department of France.
[languages] Guadeloupean Creole (gcf) is widely spoken and an important marker of cultural identity.

LABEL: Equatorial Guinea
NOTES: [languages] Equatorial Guinea is the only country in Africa with Spanish as an official language.
[languages] French and Portuguese were later added for regional integration purposes (CEMAC, CPLP).
[languages] Fang and Bubi are the most prominent local languages.

LABEL: Greece
NOTES: [languages] Turkish is officially recognized in Western Thrace as a regional language for the Muslim
minority.
[languages] Minority languages such as Albanian (sqi), Aromanian (rup), Romani (rmn), Pontic Greek (pnt),
and others are present but have no official status.
[languages] Greek Sign Language (gss) is officially recognized.
[languages] Several migrant communities, particularly from the Middle East (Arabic), English-speaking
expats, Russians, Albanians, and Kurds, are present in Greece.

LABEL: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

officialName.eng: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

NOTES: [languages] English is the official language by administrative function, despite the absence of permanent
population.
[mottos] The motto 'Leo Terram Propriam Protegat' (Latin: 'May the lion protect his own land') appears
on the territory’s coat of arms. Left as official
[currencies] No locally issued currency; British Pound (GBP) is generally accepted.
[dialCodes] Shares +500 with the Falkland Islands, though the territory lacks civilian telecom infrastructure.

LABEL: Guatemala
NOTES: [languages] Spanish is the only de jure official language.
[languages] Over 20 indigenous languages are recognized as regional languages, primarily of Mayan origin.
[mottos] The national motto appears on the coat of arms and is considered official.

LABEL: Guam
NOTES: [languages] English and Chamorro are both official languages by law.
[languages] Filipino (Tagalog) is widely spoken due to migration.
[languages] There are significant local communities speaking Japanese, Korean, and Chinese.
[mottos] Guam has dual-language motto usage: in Chamorro and English.

LABEL: Guinea-Bissau
NOTES: [languages] Portuguese is the only language with legal official status.
[languages] Crioulo (pov) is widely spoken as a lingua franca.
[languages] Several Niger-Congo languages are spoken by ethnic communities.

LABEL: Guyana

text.eng: One People, One Nation, One Destiny

NOTES: [languages] English is the sole official language and is used in government and education.
[languages] Guyanese Creole (gyn) and Hindustani (hns) are widely spoken.
[languages] Several indigenous Cariban and Arawakan languages are still spoken in rural communities.

LABEL: Hong Kong

officialName.yue-Hant: 中華人民共和國香港特別行政區
officialName.cmn-Hans: 中华人民共和国香港特别行政区

NOTES: [languages] English and Cantonese (yue) are official in practice; only English is de jure.
[languages] Mandarin (cmn) is widely spoken due to migration from mainland China.
[languages] Local communities include other Sinitic and Southeast Asian languages such as Hakka (hak), Wu (wuu), Filipino (fil), and Indonesian (ind).
[ccIdn] The IDN .香港 uses traditional Chinese script (zh-Hant).

LABEL: Heard Island and McDonald Islands
NOTES: [status] The territory is uninhabited and administered by Australia.
[ccTld] Despite its uninhabited status, the .hm domain is valid and assigned.
[dialCodes] The +6724 prefix is technically assigned but not used for general telecommunications.

LABEL: Honduras
NOTES: [languages] Spanish is the only de jure official language as per the Constitution.
[languages] Indigenous and Afro-Honduran languages (e.g., Garífuna, Lenca, Pech, Tawahka) are protected
through intercultural education programs, but do not hold formal regional official status.
[languages] Honduran Sign Language (hds) is recognized socially and used by the deaf community.

LABEL: Croatia
NOTES: [languages] Croatian is the only de jure official language of Croatia, according to its constitution.
[languages] Serbian, Italian, and Hungarian have recognized co-official status in specific municipalities
or regions, as protected minority languages.
[languages] Languages like Slovene, Czech, Romani, and Rusyn are spoken by local communities and
recognized for cultural protection.
[languages] Croatian Sign Language (hsh) is recognized by law and supported in education and public
communication.

LABEL: Haiti
NOTES: [languages] Haitian Creole (hat) and French (fra) are both official languages under the Constitution
of Haiti.
[languages] Haitian Sign Language (hsl) is in use within the deaf community, although it is not
officially recognized.

LABEL: Hungary
NOTES: [languages] Hungarian (hun) is the sole official language of Hungary, defined by the Constitution.
[languages] Several minority languages, including Serbian, Croatian, Ukrainian, Slovak, Romanian,
and Romani, enjoy regional recognition and support in municipalities where minorities exceed
legal thresholds.
[languages] Romani (rom) is present due to immigration and demographic growth and is included under
extraTerritorialCommunities.
[signs] Hungarian Sign Language (hsh) is legally recognized.

LABEL: Indonesia
NOTES: [languages] Indonesian is the only official language with legal status in the country.
[languages] Javanese, Sundanese, Minangkabau, Bugis, Balinese, Madurese, and Banjarese are widely spoken.
[languages] Acehnese, Batak, Rejang, Toraja, Sasak, Gorontalo, Berau, Komering, Tondano, and Kuri are used
by local communities.
[languages] Chinese languages like Hakka and Hokkien are spoken by long-established immigrant communities.
[languages] Mandarin is also spoken in educational or institutional settings.
[signs] Indonesian Sign Language (inl) is used in education and communication, but lacks formal recognition.
[dialCodes] +62 is officially assigned to Indonesia.

LABEL: Ireland
NOTES: [languages] Irish is the only official language de jure in the Constitution.
[languages] English is used as the primary working language of the state.
[languages] Polish is spoken by a sizable immigrant community.
[signs] Irish Sign Language (isg) is used and legally recognized in Ireland.
[dialCodes] +353 is officially assigned to Ireland.

LABEL: Israel
NOTES: [languages] Hebrew is the only official language since the 2018 Basic Law.
[languages] Arabic holds a special status and remains used in public life.
[languages] Russian, English, Amharic, and Yiddish are widely spoken.
[languages] Judaeo-Spanish, Judaeo-Aramaic, and others are used by heritage groups.
[signs] Israeli Sign Language (isr) is used but not officially recognized.
[dialCodes] +972 is officially assigned to Israel.

LABEL: Isle of Man
NOTES: [languages] English is the official language used in administration and public life.
[languages] Manx Gaelic (glv) is spoken by local communities and promoted as a cultural heritage.
[signs] British Sign Language (bfi) is used but not officially recognized.
[dialCodes] +441624 is used de facto under UK numbering plan.
Calls to Isle of Man may be routed through UK and Channel Islands due to shared prefix.

LABEL: India
NOTES: [languages] Hindi and English are the official languages at the federal level.
[languages] India has no declared national language.
[languages] 22 languages are recognized in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
[languages] Indian Sign Language (ins) is standardized and supported but not de jure official.
[dialCodes] +91 is officially assigned to India.

LABEL: British Indian Ocean Territory
NOTES: [languages] The British Indian Ocean Territory has no permanent civilian population.
English is used as the official language for administrative purposes.
No local or sign languages are in use on the territory.

LABEL: Iraq
NOTES: [languages] Arabic and Kurdish are co-official under the 2005 Constitution (Art. 4).
[languages] Turkmen, Syriac, and Armenian are regionally recognized for official use.
[dialCodes] +964 is officially assigned to Iraq.

LABEL: Iran (Islamic Republic of)
NOTES: [languages] Persian (fas) is the sole official language of the Islamic Republic of Iran.
[languages] Azerbaijani, Kurdish, Gilaki, Luri, Baluchi, and Mazanderani are regional.
[languages] Other languages like Talysh, Southern Kurdish, and Brahui are spoken locally.
[dialCodes] +98 is officially assigned to Iran.

LABEL: Iceland
NOTES: [languages] Icelandic is the only official language under national law.
[languages] English is widely spoken as a second language.
[languages] Polish and Lithuanian are spoken by immigrant communities.
[signs] Icelandic Sign Language (icl) is recognized since 2011.
[dialCodes] +354 is officially assigned to Iceland.

LABEL: Italy
NOTES: [languages] Italian is the only official language of the Republic.
[languages] German, French, Slovene, Croatian, Catalan, Friulian, Sardinian, Ladin and others are regional.
[languages] Albanian, Greek and Molise Croatian are used in local communities.
[languages] Neapolitan, Sicilian, Venetian and others are widely spoken across regions.
[signs] Italian Sign Language (ise) is used but has no formal legal recognition.
[dialCodes] +39 is officially assigned to Italy.

LABEL: Jersey
NOTES: [languages] English is the official language of Jersey.
[languages] French is widely spoken and historically used in legal contexts.
[languages] Jèrriais (nrf) is spoken by local communities and culturally promoted.
[dialCodes] +441534 is used de facto and routed under UK's numbering system.
[dialCodes] Calls from UK, Guernsey, or Isle of Man use 01534 as local area code.

LABEL: Jamaica
NOTES: [languages] English is the only official language of Jamaica.
[languages] Jamaican Patois (jam) is widely spoken in daily life.
[dialCodes] +1876 and +1658 are officially assigned to Jamaica.

LABEL: Jordan
NOTES: [languages] Arabic is the only official language of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan.
[languages] English is widely used in education, business, and public signage.
[languages] Minority languages include Kurdish, Azerbaijani, Armenian, Aramaic, Chechen, Circassian.
[dialCodes] +962 is officially assigned to Jordan.

LABEL: Japan
NOTES: [languages] Japanese is the national language de facto, without constitutional status.
[languages] Ryukyuan and Ainu are indigenous languages with cultural recognition.
[languages] Korean, Chinese, and English are spoken by immigrant communities.
[signs] Japanese Sign Language (jsl) is used but lacks formal ISO recognition.
[dialCodes] +81 is officially assigned to Japan.

LABEL: Kenya
NOTES: [languages] English and Swahili are co-official per Constitution (Article 7).
[languages] Kikuyu, Luo, Kamba, Kalenjin, Meru are widely spoken across regions.
[languages] Gujarati, Maasai, Somali and others are used in local communities.
[signs] Kenyan Sign Language (ksl) is used in education and everyday communication.
[dialCodes] +254 is officially assigned to Kenya.
[dialCodes] 020 may be used for Kenya from Tanzania or Uganda in legacy routes.
[dialCodes] Historical East African telephone network allowed cross-border direct dialing with shared prefixes.

LABEL: Kyrgyzstan
NOTES: [languages] Kirghiz is the State language as defined by the Constitution.
[languages] Russian is official for interethnic communication and used widely in public life.
[languages] Uzbek is widely spoken in the south, especially in Osh and Jalal-Abad regions.
[languages] Other minority languages include Uyghur, Tatar, Tajik, and Hazara varieties.

LABEL: Cambodia

officialName.khm: ព្រះរាជាណាចក្រ កម្ពុជា

text.khm: ជាតិ សាសនា ព្រះមហាក្សត្រ

NOTES: [languages] Khmer is the sole official language of Cambodia (Constitution, Article 5).
[languages] Vietnamese, Chinese, French, and English are commonly spoken in cities and trade.
[languages] Many indigenous Austroasiatic languages are spoken by rural minorities in eastern regions.
[signs] Cambodian Sign Language (csn) is in use and supported by local deaf education programs.
[dialCodes] +855 is officially assigned to Cambodia.

LABEL: Kiribati

text.gil: Te mauri, te raoi ao te tabomoa

NOTES: [languages] English and Gilbertese (gil) are co-official languages of Kiribati.
[languages] English is primarily used in administration and education.
[dialCodes] +686 is the official calling code for Kiribati.
[timeZones] The country spans three time zones, including UTC+14 (Kiritimati).

LABEL: Comoros
NOTES: [languages] Comorian (swb), French and Arabic are co-official languages under the Constitution.
[mottos] The official motto is only attested in Arabic: وحدة، تضامن، تنمية.

LABEL: Saint Kitts and Nevis

officialName.eng: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis

NOTES: [languages] English is the sole official language. Jamaican Creole (jam) is widely spoken.
[mottos] 'Country Above Self' is the official motto of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

LABEL: Korea (Democratic People's Republic of)
NOTES: [languages] Korean is the sole official language of the DPRK.
[mottos] '강성대국' ('Strong and Prosperous Nation') is a core ideological slogan.

LABEL: Korea (Republic of)
NOTES: [languages] Korean is the sole de jure official language of South Korea.
[languages] English is widely taught and used in education, business, and signage.
[languages] Chinese (zho) is spoken by a historical community established in Korea for over a century.
[languages] Vietnamese, Filipino, Uzbek, Mongolian and Thai are spoken by immigrant communities.
[signs] Korean Sign Language (kvk) is officially recognized since 2016.

LABEL: Kuwait
NOTES: [languages] Arabic is the only official language of Kuwait.
[languages] English is widely used in business, education and as a second language.
[languages] Significant expatriate communities speak Persian, Hindi, Urdu, Tagalog, Malayalam, Bengali,
Tamil, Telugu and Nepali.
[languages] Urdu represents a large extra-territorial community due to longstanding Pakistani immigration,
though it is not yet transmitted natively within Kuwait.
[languages] Gulf Arabic (afb) is the main local dialect spoken natively.

LABEL: Cayman Islands

text.eng: He hath founded it upon the seas

NOTES: [languages] English is the official language of the Cayman Islands.
[languages] Cayman Creole English is spoken informally but lacks official recognition.

LABEL: Kazakhstan
NOTES: [languages] Kazakh is the state language as defined by the Constitution.
[languages] Russian is widely spoken and has official status for interethnic communication.
[languages] Local communities speak Uzbek, Uyghur, Tatar, Ukrainian, Korean and German.
[dialCodes] Kazakhstan adopted +997 in 2023, but +7 remains widely used during transition.
[languages] Uzbekistan and Russia account for the majority of recent migrant inflows, but no immigrant
group exceeds 1% individually.

LABEL: Lao People's Democratic Republic

officialName.lao: ສາທາລະນະລັດ ປະຊາທິປະໄຕ ປະຊາຊົນລາວ

text.lao: ສັນຕິພາບ ເອກະລາດ ປະຊາທິປະໄຕ ເອກະພາບ ວັດທະນະຖາວອນ

NOTES: [languages] Lao is the only official language of Laos (Article 89 of the Constitution).
[languages] Khmer, Hmong, Thai, Vietnamese and other minority languages are spoken in border or rural areas.
[languages] Central Thai (cth) and Brao (blr) are present in specific ethnolinguistic pockets.

LABEL: Lebanon
NOTES: [languages] Arabic is the only official language of Lebanon (Article 11 of the Constitution).
[languages] French and English are widely used in education, media and commerce.
[languages] Armenian, Syriac and Kurdish are present among local ethnolinguistic communities.
[languages] North Levantine Arabic (acm) is the dominant spoken dialect.

LABEL: Saint Lucia

text.eng: The Land, The People, The Light

NOTES: [languages] English is the only official language of Saint Lucia.
[languages] Saint Lucian Creole French (acf) is widely spoken and culturally significant.

LABEL: Liechtenstein
NOTES: [languages] German (deu) is the sole official language of Liechtenstein.
[languages] Walser German (wae) is spoken in Triesenberg and considered a living cultural heritage.
[languages] Swiss German (gsw) is the main spoken dialect throughout the country.

LABEL: Sri Lanka
NOTES: [languages] Sinhala and Tamil are both official languages of Sri Lanka.
[languages] English is recognized for official and educational use.
[languages] Sanskrit and Urdu are spoken within religious and minority contexts.

LABEL: Liberia

text.eng: The Love of Liberty Brought Us Here

NOTES: [languages] English is the sole official language of Liberia.
[languages] Liberian Kreyol (lir) is widely spoken as a lingua franca.
[languages] Numerous indigenous languages are actively spoken in local communities.

LABEL: Lesotho
NOTES: [languages] Sesotho and English are co-official languages of Lesotho.
[languages] Zulu and Xhosa are spoken by local communities near the southern border.

LABEL: Lithuania
NOTES: [languages] Lithuanian is the sole official language (Constitution, Article 14).
[languages] Russian is widely spoken among the ethnic minority communities.
[languages] Polish, Belarusian, Ukrainian, and Romani are used locally, especially in border regions.

LABEL: Luxembourg

text.ltz: Mir wëlle bleiwe wat mir sinn
text.fra: Nous voulons rester ce que nous sommes
text.deu: Wir wollen bleiben, was wir sind

NOTES: [languages] Luxembourgish, French, and German are official languages under the 1984 language law.
[languages] Portuguese, Italian, and English are spoken by significant expatriate communities.

LABEL: Latvia
NOTES: [languages] Latvian is the sole official language. Russian is widely spoken, especially in urban areas.
[languages] Ukrainian, Belarusian, Polish, and Romani are spoken by minority communities.

LABEL: Libya
NOTES: [languages] Arabic is the sole official language in Libya.
[languages] Tamazight varieties (tzm, taq, zgh) are spoken by Berber communities.
[languages] Domari (itk) is spoken by itinerant groups; Nafusi Arabic (ayl) is the main dialect in the west.

LABEL: Morocco
NOTES: [languages] Arabic and Standard Amazigh are the only de jure official languages.
[languages] French is widely used in administration, education, and media.
[languages] Riffian, Central Atlas Tamazight, and Shilha are used by local Amazigh communities.
[languages] Spanish is used by some communities, mainly in the north and Western Sahara.
[dialCodes] +212 is the official dial code assigned to Morocco.
[mottos] The national motto 'God, Homeland, King' exists in both Arabic and Amazigh versions.

LABEL: Monaco
NOTES: [languages] French is the only official language by constitutional law.
[languages] Italian and English are widely spoken due to geographic and economic context.
[languages] Ligurian and Occitan are used by local historical communities.
[mottos] 'Deo Juvante' is the official motto of Monaco in Latin.
[dialCodes] +377 is the de jure telephone code assigned to Monaco.

LABEL: Moldova (Republic of)
NOTES: [languages] Romanian is the only de jure official language.
[languages] Russian is widely spoken, especially in Transnistria and Gagauzia.
[languages] Ukrainian, Bulgarian, and Gagauz are used by local communities.
[dialCodes] +373 is the de jure telephone code assigned to Moldova.
[timeZones] Europe/Tiraspol is used de facto in the Transnistria region.

LABEL: Montenegro
NOTES: [languages] Montenegrin is the only de jure official language.
[languages] Serbian, Bosnian, Croatian, and Albanian are widely spoken.
[mottos] 'Čast i Sloboda' is the official national motto in Montenegrin (Latin and Cyrillic).
[dialCodes] +382 is the de jure telephone code assigned to Montenegro.
[localesIcu] ICU locales reflect the bilingual Latin-Cyrillic usage of Serbian variants.

LABEL: Saint Martin (French part)
NOTES: [languages] French is the only de jure official language.
[languages] English is widely spoken across the island.
[languages] Haitian Creole and Norman are used in local communities.
[languages] Spanish is spoken by extraterritorial immigrant communities.
[dialCodes] +590 is assigned under French jurisdiction and used in Saint Martin.

LABEL: Madagascar
NOTES: [languages] Malagasy and French are the two official languages by constitutional law.
[mottos] 'Tanindrazana, Fahafahana, Fandrosoana' is the official motto in Malagasy.
[dialCodes] +261 is the de jure telephone code assigned to Madagascar.
[localesIcu] French and English ICU locales are supported for Madagascar.
[ccTld] .mg is the assigned country code top-level domain for Madagascar.

LABEL: Marshall Islands
NOTES: [languages] Marshallese and English are the official languages by constitutional law.

LABEL: North Macedonia
NOTES: [languages] Macedonian and Albanian are de jure official languages.
[languages] Romani, Turkish, Serbian, Vlach, and Bosnian are used in local communities.
[localesIcu] ICU locales support both Macedonian and Albanian for North Macedonia.

LABEL: Mali

text.fra: Un peuple, un but, une foi

NOTES: [languages] French is the only official language by constitutional law.
[languages] Bambara and Pular are widely spoken across the country.
[languages] Soninke, Songhay, Tamasheq, Dyula, and others are used in local communities.

LABEL: Myanmar

officialName.mya: ပြည်ထောင်စု သမ္မတ မြန်မာနိုင်ငံတော်

NOTES: [languages] Burmese is the only official language by constitutional law.
[languages] Shan, Karen, Mon, Rakhine, and others are spoken in local communities.
[languages] Mandarin Chinese and Tamil are spoken by communities over the 1% threshold.
[dialCodes] +95 is the de jure telephone code assigned to Myanmar.
[timeZones] Both Asia/Yangon and the deprecated Asia/Rangoon are in use.

LABEL: Mongolia
NOTES: [languages] Mongolian is the only official language by constitutional law.
[languages] Russian is still widely taught and used, though not official.
[languages] Kazakh, Tuvan, Buryat, and Darkhad are spoken by native local communities.
[ccIdn] .мон is the IDN ccTLD in Mongolian Cyrillic.

LABEL: Macao

officialName.cmn-Hans: 中华人民共和国澳门特别行政区
officialName.yue-Hant: 中華人民共和國澳門特別行政區
officialName.por: Região Administrativa Especial de Macau da República Popular da China

NOTES: [languages] Yue Chinese (Cantonese) and Portuguese are the only official languages by Basic Law.
[languages] Mandarin Chinese is widely spoken but not official.
[languages] English is used in local communities, especially in business and tourism.
[dialCodes] +853 is the de jure telephone code assigned to Macao.
[officialName] Names reflect official designation in Mandarin (Hans), Cantonese (Hant), and Portuguese.

LABEL: Northern Mariana Islands

officialName.eng: Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands

NOTES: [languages] English, Chamorro, and Carolinian are the official languages by local constitution.
[languages] Filipino, Japanese, and Korean are spoken by local communities.
[dependency] The territory is a commonwealth in political union with the United States.

LABEL: Martinique
NOTES: [languages] French is the only official language by French national law.
[languages] Antillean Creole French is widely spoken among the population.
[languages] Haitian Creole and Island Carib are used in some local communities.
[dialCodes] +596 is the de jure telephone code assigned to Martinique.
[dependency] Martinique is an overseas territorial collectivity of France.

LABEL: Mauritania
NOTES: [languages] Arabic is the only official language by constitutional law.
[languages] French, Hassaniya Arabic, and Zenaga are widely spoken.
[languages] Soninke, Pulaar, Serer, and Bissa are used in local communities.
[dialCodes] +222 is the de jure telephone code assigned to Mauritania.
[mottos] 'شرف إخاء عدل' (Honor, Fraternity, Justice) is the official national motto in Arabic.

LABEL: Montserrat

text.eng: A people of excellence, moulded by nature, nurtured by God

NOTES: [languages] English is the only official language by constitutional status.
[languages] Antillean Creole is used in local communities.
[dependency] Montserrat is a British Overseas Territory.

LABEL: Mauritius
NOTES: [languages] English is the only de jure official language by law in Mauritius.
[languages] French, Mauritian Creole, and Bhojpuri are widely spoken.
[languages] South Asian languages such as Urdu, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, and Caribbean Hindustani
are used in local communities.
[languages] Yue Chinese is spoken by Chinese diaspora communities over the 1% threshold.

LABEL: Maldives
NOTES: [languages] Dhivehi is the only official language by constitutional law.
[languages] English is widely used in education, tourism, and administration.
[languages] Hindi and Tamil are spoken by migrant worker communities.

LABEL: Malawi
NOTES: [languages] Chichewa (Nyanja) and English are the two official languages of Malawi.
[languages] Tumbuka and Yao are widely spoken across several regions.
[languages] Lozi, Tswana, Tonga, and Sena are spoken in local communities.

LABEL: Mexico
NOTES: [languages] Mexico recognizes 68 indigenous languages as national languages per LGDLPI (2003).
Only Spanish has nationwide functional official status.
[languages] Regional indigenous languages include Nahuatl, Mixtec, Zapotec, Maya, Tarahumara, and others.
[signs] Mexican Sign Language (mfs) is officially recognized nationally.

LABEL: Malaysia
NOTES: [languages] Malaysia recognizes Malay (zsm) as the only official language according to Article 152 of the
Constitution.
English, Mandarin Chinese (zho), and Tamil (tam) are widely used in education, media, and commerce.
Indigenous groups and migrant communities speak various local languages including Telugu (tel),
Banjar (bjn), Temiar (tem), and others.
[languages] The Malay language also has a different alphabet called 'Jawi', which does not have a
corresponding ISO 639 code. IGNORED.

LABEL: Mozambique
NOTES: [languages] Portuguese is the only official language. Bantu languages are widely used in local communities.
[languages] Makhuwa, Sena, and Tswa-related languages are the most spoken native languages across regions.

LABEL: Namibia
NOTES: [languages] English is the only official language.
[languages] Afrikaans, German, Khoekhoe, Herero, and Lozi are widely spoken regionally.
[languages] Several San and Bantu languages are spoken by indigenous communities.

LABEL: New Caledonia
NOTES: [languages] French is the only official language. Kanak languages like Ajië and Drehu are used in local education.
[languages] Over 30 Kanak languages are recognized as heritage. Several have ISO codes and active speakers.
[languages] Hmong Njua (hnj) is spoken by a Lao Hmong community in Bourail, active since 1975.

LABEL: Niger
NOTES: [languages] French is the only official language. Hausa and Tamajeq are widely used regionally.
[languages] Kanuri, Fulani, and Djerma-Songhai are major language groups.
[languages] Local communities use a range of indigenous languages including Bomu, Mafa, and Serer.

LABEL: Norfolk Island
NOTES: [languages] Norfuk is legally protected and used locally, but lacks an ISO 639-3 code. Excluded.
[mottos] Motto 'Inasmuch' is in Norfuk. No ISO code exists, so stored using key 'und' in mottos.official.

text.eng: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress

LABEL: Nicaragua
NOTES: [languages] 'ncs' (Nicaraguan Sign Language) is recognized and used especially in the capital and among
Deaf communities.
[languages] Miskito (miq), Mayangna (ulw), and Creole English variants have co-official or recognized
status in the Atlantic Coast autonomous regions.

LABEL: Netherlands
NOTES: [languages] Dutch Sign Language (dse) has been officially recognized since 2020.
[languages] Papiamento (pap) is co-official in the Caribbean Netherlands (Bonaire, Saba, Sint Eustatius).
[languages] English is widely used in higher education, media, and business, but has no official status
and is not considered 'widely spoken' under national linguistic policy.
[languages] Frisian (fry) is co-official in Friesland province.

LABEL: Norway
NOTES: [languages] Norwegian Bokmål (nob) and Nynorsk (nno) are the two written standards of Norwegian.
[languages] Sami languages (sme, smj, sma) are co-official in designated municipalities in northern Norway.
[languages] Norwegian Sign Language (nsl) is recognized under the Norwegian Education Act (1997).
[languages] Kven (fkv), Romani (rmy), and Traveller Rodi (rme) are recognized regional minority languages.
[languages] Polish (pol), Somali (som), Urdu (urd), and Arabic (ara) are spoken by large immigrant communities, but not considered widely spoken nationally.

LABEL: Nepal
NOTES: [languages] Nepali is the only official language by constitutional provision.
[languages] Maithili, Bhojpuri, Newar, Tamang, Magar, Awadhi, and Tharu are widely spoken.
[languages] Doteli, Limbu, Sanskrit, Chepang, Sunuwar, and Byangsi are used in local communities.
[dialCodes] +977 is the official and exclusive international dial code for Nepal.
[timeZones] 'Asia/Katmandu' is a deprecated alias; only 'Asia/Kathmandu' should be used.

LABEL: Nauru
NOTES: [languages] Nauruan and English are both official languages by law.

LABEL: New Zealand
NOTES: [languages] English, Māori and New Zealand Sign Language are official languages by law.
[languages] Māori is also spoken as part of historical indigenous communities.
[languages] Samoan, Tongan, and Kurdish are widely spoken due to migration.
[languages] Mandarin, Hindi, and Tagalog are spoken by large migrant communities.
[dialCodes] +64 is the official international dial code for New Zealand.

LABEL: Oman
NOTES: [languages] Arabic is the only official language according to the constitution.
[languages] Gulf Arabic (afb) is the main spoken variety, not official.
[languages] Balochi and Comorian are widely spoken minority languages.
[languages] English and Hindi are spoken by local communities and expatriates.
[dialCodes] +968 is the official international dial code for Oman.

LABEL: Panama
NOTES: [languages] Spanish is the only official language of Panama.
[languages] Indigenous languages like Guna (gnb, gna), Emberá (ebr), and others are used by native communities.
[currencies] Bitcoin is legal for optional use in Panama, but not legal tender;
constitutional issues blocked related legislation.
Anyway there is no ISO code for bitcoin.

LABEL: Peru

text.spa: Firme y feliz por la unión

NOTES: [languages] Spanish is the only nationwide official language of Peru.
[languages] Quechua and Aymara are official regionally and added under 'regional'.
[languages] Several Amazonian languages (agr, cni, shp, mrc, ash) are used by indigenous communities.

LABEL: French Polynesia
NOTES: [languages] French is the only official language under French jurisdiction.
[languages] Tahitian, Pa'umotu, North Marquesan, and South Marquesan are used by native communities.
[mottos] 'Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité' is the official French motto.
[mottos] 'Pōrīnetia Farāni' is a popular local rendering in Tahitian.

LABEL: Papua New Guinea

officialName.eng: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
officialName.hmo: Independen Stet bilong Papua Niu Gini

NOTES: [languages] English and Hiri Motu are the only official languages by law.
[languages] Tok Pisin (tpi) is widely spoken but lacks formal official status.
[languages] Motu (meu) and Kagua (kag) are used by local indigenous communities.

LABEL: Philippines

text.eng: For God, People, Nature and Country

NOTES: [languages] Filipino and English are the only official languages by law.
[languages] Tagalog, Cebuano, Ilocano and Hiligaynon are widely spoken.
[languages] Waray, Bicol, Maguindanao, Tausug and Maranao are used in local communities.
[languages] Bukusu and Masbate are spoken by migrant communities and classified as extra-territorial.
[dialCodes] +63 is the official international dial code assigned to the Philippines.
[mottos] Motto is recognized officially in both Tagalog and English versions.

LABEL: Pakistan
NOTES: [languages] Urdu is the only official language by law.
[languages] Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto, and Balochi are official at provincial level or widely spoken.
[languages] Seraiki, Marwari, Gujarati, and Kashmiri are spoken by local communities.
[languages] Hindi and Brahui are used by migrant or border-crossing communities.

LABEL: Poland
NOTES: [languages] Polish is the only official language by law.
[languages] Silesian is spoken locally but not officially recognized.

LABEL: Russian Federation
NOTES: [languages] Russian (rus) is the only de jure official language.

NOTES: [languages] Kinyarwanda (kin), English, French and Swahili are all de jure official languages by constitutional law.

LABEL: Solomon Islands

NOTES: [languages] Singapore has four de jure official languages: Malay (msa), English (eng), Mandarin Chinese
(cmn), and Tamil (tam).

[languages] Extra-territorial communities include Bengali (ben), Urdu (urd), Telugu (tel), and Hindi (hin)
due to migrant labor population.
